samples.summary: The read-only image-copy outcome the change is built around is unreachable: `handleImageMouseDown` bails on `readOnly`, so a viewer can never click-select an image
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` begins with `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2497), so in a read-only document no mousedown ever reaches `selectImageInline(hit.blockId, hit.offset)` (2550). Yet the new `selectImageInline` helper's doc comment (editor.ts:1241-1256) and docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:251-259 justify the added `textEditorRef?.focus()` entirely by "a clicked image on a read-only document ... the context menu's read-only Copy entry", and the new test 'a read-only viewer can copy a click-selected image' only reaches that state through the programmatic `editor.selectImageAt()` API. Grepping packages/frontend/src finds no caller of `selectImageAt` at all, so in production the read-only image copy path described by the design doc cannot be entered. Either the mousedown guard needs to allow selection in read-only (selection mutates nothing), or the doc/rationale overstates what ships.

samples.summary: The context menu still cannot offer Copy for a click-selected image — its `hasSelection` is a text selection only, so the image branch of the new copy path is never reachable from the menu
samples.evidence: `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (docs-context-menu.tsx:74) and `getActiveSelection()` (editor.ts:3233-3249) returns null unless `selection.range` is a non-collapsed *text* range. `selectImageInline` explicitly does `selection.setRange(null)`, so with an image selected the menu computes `hasSelection === false`, hides Copy, and (in read-only) does not even open. The new design-doc text (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:256-258) asserts the opposite — that "the context menu's read-only Copy entry" is what makes the image copy path matter. The keyboard path works; the menu path claimed by the change does not, so a user who right-clicks a selected image still gets no Copy.

samples.summary: The canonical context-menu design doc was not updated for the read-only Copy behaviour change, and now contradicts the code
samples.evidence: The change makes Copy visible in read-only (`showCopy = hasSelection`) and lets the clipboard group open in read-only (`hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection`). docs/design/docs/docs-context-menu.md still describes the group as "**Cut / Copy** (selection-gated) and **Paste**" (line 22) and states the menu "returns without opening if every group is empty (so read-only / nothing-to-offer right-clicks show neither an overlay nor the native menu)" (lines 56-59), which is now false for a read-only right-click over a selection. The image doc was updated but this one — the doc that owns the behaviour being changed — was not.

samples.summary: The issue #872 half of the change (copying inside a table cell) is recorded in no design doc; the canonical table-clipboard doc is left stale
samples.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` is rewritten to resolve cell blocks via `blockParentMap` + `resolveNestedTableLayout` — a real change to how the copy path resolves a range, and the one that fixes #872. docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md is the canonical doc for Docs table clipboard (it documents the `handleCopy`/`handleCut` cell branch and even a future phase that says "extend `getSelectedBlocks()`", line 237), and it is untouched by this change. The #870 half got a thorough doc update in docs-image-editing.md; the #872 half got none, so the repo's record of the copy path stays wrong.

samples.summary: The new cell-resolution + `sliceBlockRange` is a third independent traversal of "which blocks does a DocRange cover", duplicating the module the repo built to be the only one
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts opens with "The one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers" and explains it exists so the read and write sides cannot diverge (issue #715). Its `visitRangeSlices` already implements exactly the cases the new code re-implements: same-block, cross-block-inside-one-cell (resolving the cell via `doc.blockParentMap` and the table block's `tableData.rows[..].cells[..]`, lines 162-190), and top-level cross-block. `selection.ts:264-291` holds a further copy for text extraction. The new `getSelectedBlocks()` branch adds a fourth variant against `layout.blockParentMap`/`resolveNestedTableLayout` that intentionally differs — it resolves nested-table cells, which `visitRangeSlices` documents as deliberately unsupported (range-slices.ts:139-143). The clipboard and the styling/dirty-marking paths now answer "which blocks does this range cover" differently for nested tables, which is precisely the divergence range-slices.ts was created to prevent.

samples.summary: The image copy writes only the internal `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` flavour and alt text, so copying an image still pastes nothing usable outside the app
samples.evidence: `writeImageToClipboard` sets `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` and `text/plain` = `image.alt ?? ''`. Pasting the copied image into any other application yields an empty string (or the alt text). If issue #870's acceptance is "Cmd+C over a selected image copies the image", the intra-document case is met but the cross-application case is not, and no `text/html` (``) flavour — which would be cheap given `ImageData.src` is a loadable URL — is written. Flagging as a possible unmet acceptance criterion since the issue text was not supplied.

samples.summary: Two unrelated issues (#870 image clipboard, #872 table-cell copy) are fixed in one change, spanning three packages and one design doc that covers only half of it
samples.evidence: The diff mixes the image-selection clipboard work (#870, editor.ts + text-editor.ts hooks + frontend context menu + docs-image-editing.md) with an independent `getSelectedBlocks()` rewrite for table-cell copy (#872, documented nowhere). They share only the file `text-editor.ts`. Splitting would let each land against its own design doc; as filed, the #872 change rides in with no spec record and the doc update covers only #870.

samples.summary: Object Replacement Character written as a literal glyph instead of the `'￼'` escape used everywhere else in the package
samples.evidence: Every other production site spells it `'￼'` (model/types.ts:121,453; import/docx-parser.ts:69; view/editor.ts:3670). `writeImageToClipboard` uses the raw character `'￼'`, which is invisible in most editors and diffs; the neighbouring comment even misspells it "ORC".

Yet the new `selectImageInline` helper's doc comment (editor.ts:1241-1256) and docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:251-259 justify the added `textEditorRef?.focus()` entirely by "a clicked image on a read-only document ... the context menu's read-only Copy entry", and the new test 'a read-only viewer can copy a click-selected image' only reaches that state through the programmatic `editor.selectImageAt()` API. verdict.reason: Every claim checks out against the tree. `handleImageMouseDown` starts with `if (readOnly) return;` (editor.ts:2497) before any hit-test, so the `selectImageInline(hit.blockId, hit.offset)` call at editor.ts:2550 can never run on a read-only document. `selectImageInline` (editor.ts:1255-1259) is the only site that assigns a non-null `selectedImage` (grep of `selectedImage = ` shows 1257 as the sole non-null assignment), and its only other entry point is the `selectImageAt` EditorAPI method (editor.ts:317, 3681-3687), for which grep across packages/frontend finds zero callers — the only callers repo-wide are packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts. `readOnly` is fixed at editor construction (editor.ts:919, docs-view.tsx:327), so no selection can carry over from an editable session. Meanwhile the new doc comment (editor.ts:1241-1253) and docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:251-259 justify the added `textEditorRef?.focus()` entirely by a read-only click-selected image and "the context menu's read-only Copy entry" — and that context menu's Copy is itself gated on a *text* selection (docs-context-menu.tsx:74, 181), with the task doc conceding image support in context-menu Copy/Cut is still a gap (20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:171). So the design doc and the task doc's third-round bullet (lines 198-203) document a user-facing outcome that does not ship. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, the readOnly guard is the defect rather than something that makes it moot, and spec-conformance/design-doc accuracy is in this lens's lane. Whether the cost is major or minor is arguable, and that uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: The context menu still cannot offer Copy for a click-selected image — its `hasSelection` is a text selection only, so the image branch of the new copy path is never reachable from the menu
finding.evidence: `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (docs-context-menu.tsx:74) and `getActiveSelection()` (editor.ts:3233-3249) returns null unless `selection.range` is a non-collapsed *text* range. `selectImageInline` explicitly does `selection.setRange(null)`, so with an image selected the menu computes `hasSelection === false`, hides Copy, and (in read-only) does not even open. The new design-doc text (docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:256-258) asserts the opposite — that "the context menu's read-only Copy entry" is what makes the image copy path matter. The keyboard path works; the menu path claimed by the change does not, so a user who right-clicks a selected image still gets no Copy.

verdict.reason: The mechanical facts check out: docs-context-menu.tsx:74 gates Copy on `!!editor.getActiveSelection()` (line 181, plus the read-only open-bail at 80/84), editor.ts:3233-3241 returns null for anything but a non-collapsed text range, and selectImageInline (editor.ts:1255-1259) clears the range — so the menu indeed offers no Copy for a click-selected image, and I found no counterexample surface anywhere in the Docs frontend (DocsContextMenu is wired once at docs-view.tsx:615; the image-aware menu entry at sheet-context-menu.tsx:234 is Sheets). But this is not blocking under the design-fit rubric: no acceptance criterion requires it. The originating task's criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:51-62) are the keyboard Cmd/Ctrl+C image paths plus "Read-only Copy is offered in the context menu (it always worked)", which is the text-selection Copy and is delivered and tested (docs-context-menu.test.tsx:93-127). The same task doc explicitly defers this exact item at line 171: "image support in the context menu's Copy/Cut (a real gap, but a separate change)". The stated user outcome for #870 (copy a click-selected image, including read-only) works via the keyboard/`copy`-event path the diff fixes. What is left is an over-claiming rationale sentence in docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:255-259 — design-doc drift whose cost stays inside the codebase, i.e. minor, which never blocks.
